Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Israel rejects Turkey's move to seek an Interpol red notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla case, calling it a 'pathetic attempt' to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu calls President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'.
Former French and British ambassadors urge Paris and London to take joint action on the Palestinian territories, where violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank has surged since the Gaza war began.

Israel says it fired at a 'terrorist' in southern Syria; Syria's foreign ministry says an Israeli drone hit a civilian car near Beit Jinn, west of Damascus, calling it a 'blatant violation' of Syrian sovereignty. Syrian state TV reports one person injured. It is the second Israeli strike in Syria in a week, after the Abu al-Duhur airbase attack the US called an 'unnecessary escalation'.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Israeli military, Syrian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: The Straits Times reports that the widening confrontation between Israel and Turkey could reshape the region, with Syria - which physically separates the two - bearing the brunt of their rivalry.

Syria's government condemns the Israeli strike on the village of Beit Jinn, south-west of Damascus, as a violation of its sovereignty and of international law; officials say it hit a civilian vehicle and injured several people. The Israeli military says it targeted a 'terrorist' in the 'final stages' of preparing attacks posing an immediate threat to its soldiers.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Syrian officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack says the earlier Israeli strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase could be 'the Israelis baiting the Turks' in an attempt to draw Ankara into a conflict. Washington had already called that strike an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani says he expects security talks with Israel to resume soon despite an absence of trust, with Damascus seeking an Israeli withdrawal from Syrian land and an end to strikes. He says the US is pressing Israel to return to negotiations, and denies Syria allowed Turkish forces at the airbase Israel bombed this week.

Syria and Israel hold high-level US-mediated talks in Jordan, focused on practical mechanisms to halt Israeli strikes, arrests and targeted operations and on reviving negotiations towards a security agreement, Syria's state news agency SANA reports citing a diplomatic source. Israel's prime minister's office did not comment.

At the Jordan talks, Damascus says its immediate priorities remain an Israeli withdrawal to positions held before Bashar al-Assad's overthrow on 8 Dec 2024 and full restoration of the 1974 disengagement agreement, and that it will not accept limits on rebuilding its armed forces, according to SANA.

Syrian state news agency SANA reports that Syria and Israel held further US-mediated talks aimed at easing tensions, following the round held in Jordan on 23 August. Israel's prime minister's office has not commented.

Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz warned of 'forceful actions' after four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, about 800m from the Gaza boundary, and several more elsewhere in southern Israel. The Israeli military said the kites carried no suspicious materials and posed no threat. Hamas denied responsibility, called them 'basically children's toys from displacement camps', and accused Israel of using them as a pretext for continued strikes despite the ceasefire agreed last October.
Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked a ship off Saudi Arabia's Yanbu. There was no Saudi confirmation of the claim.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli fire killed two young children. The account comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, and removed Hayat Tahrir al-Sham from its list of global terrorist organisations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it recognised Damascus distancing itself from international terrorism; Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani called it a 'historic step'. Syria remains at the centre of tension between Israel and Turkey.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Syria 'shakes off a dark stain and tears away a painful chapter of its past' after the US removed the country from its state-sponsors-of-terrorism list, thanking President Trump. The Treasury announced corresponding sanctions relief; Hayat Tahrir al-Sham was also delisted as a global terrorist organisation.

Far-right Israeli lawmaker and settler activist Zvi Sukkot took a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in Madama in the northern occupied West Bank while under military escort. The army said the demolition was unauthorised and a misuse of security protection, that soldiers stopped it and removed him, and that it viewed the incident with 'utmost severity'; Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot also criticised him.

Parents in Gaza were urged to stop children flying kites after Israel's warning to Hamas over kites found near the boundary. Israel's defence minister had threatened 'forceful actions'; the Israeli military says the kites carried nothing dangerous and Hamas calls them children's toys.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli attacks killed five people including two children. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

An official on President Trump's US-led 'Board of Peace' said all militant activity in Gaza must stop, including the flying of kites, and added that 'Israel, too, must comply with the ceasefire' and that military action cannot extend beyond genuine and imminent threats. The UN and Hamas called the kite warnings outrageous.

Israeli forces took control of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training centre between Kafr Aqab in east Jerusalem and the Qalandia refugee camp. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said the evacuation followed the law Israel passed severing ties with the agency; UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the raid. The centre, opened in 1952, trains about 340 West Bank Palestinians a year.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UNRWA, Israeli PM's office)

timeline.event: Syria's Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announced their dissolution as part of an agreed integration into the Damascus government's structures.
President Trump sent a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, while saying Riyadh must recognise Israel.
Israeli forces have taken control of a UN training centre for Palestinians, The Straits Times reports. UNRWA has not said whether courses there will continue.

Israel's seizure of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training college in East Jerusalem drew international condemnation. Israel's government says the site was evacuated lawfully; UNRWA disputes the basis for the takeover.
A far-right Israeli lawmaker damaged a Palestinian memorial with a sledgehammer, footage of the incident showed.
Lebanon accused Israel of setting fire to forest and farmland in the south of the country. Israel has not commented on the accusation.
US Senate Democrats urged Israel to rein in settler violence in the West Bank.
Turkey said the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces would help Syrian unity, a day after the SDF announced it was integrating into Damascus government structures.

The United States designated the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation and imposed sanctions on it. The group has previously said its actions target arms manufacturing sites.
An Israeli court acquitted, on grounds of mental health, the man filmed on CCTV attacking a nun in Jerusalem.
A funeral was held in the West Bank for Sliman Mansour, one of the best-known Palestinian artists of his generation.

Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials in Gaza said. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented.

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's envoy for Gaza, criticised both Israeli strikes and Hamas's actions and warned that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be 'a point of no return' for the region.

The UN human rights office condemned the United States' designation of the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation, saying the label risks criminalising protest. The State Department announced the designation, with sanctions, on 26 August.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights)

timeline.event: A former British-Israeli hostage held by Hamas married in Tel Aviv, in one of the more visible personal milestones since last October's ceasefire.
An Israeli air strike killed a Hamas operative and two other people near Jenin in the occupied West Bank, the Israeli military said, in a rare use of air power in the territory.
The BBC published the results of a week spent tracking settler violence in the occupied West Bank, documenting incidents against Palestinian communities.

Druze factions blocked students from sitting examinations in a dispute with the Syrian government, The Straits Times reported, the latest friction between Damascus and communities in the south as the new government consolidates control.

Dozens of Israeli settlers attack the Palestinian village of Qusra near Nablus in the northern occupied West Bank, residents and the Israeli military say. A resident tells AFP a small group approached villagers working on a house, then returned with dozens more, surrounded them and threw stones. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the attack, a rare step; Israeli forces deploy to the site.

Israel's military says it struck a Hamas commander "hiding within the compound" of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, saying medical facilities must not be used for militant activity. Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes elsewhere in the territory killed four people. Both accounts are contested and not independently verified.
Druze factions in southern Syria block students from sitting state examinations in a dispute with the Damascus government, The Straits Times reports.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the settler attack on the West Bank village of Qusra, calling it a criminal act that does not represent Israeli society; the Israeli military says it has opened an investigation. Palestinian residents say the village had been under a supply blockade for weeks before the attack.

The Straits Times reports that killings of Palestinian children and teenagers by Israeli forces and settlers have risen sharply in the occupied West Bank this year. Israel says its forces operate against militants; the two accounts of individual incidents frequently diverge and are rarely independently adjudicated.

An Israeli air strike near a bakery in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza kills a man and a three-year-old boy and wounds several others, Gaza health officials say; the Israeli military says it attacked a Hamas militant. Gazan health officials say more than 1,300 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Both tallies come from parties to the conflict.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters, Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: An AFP investigation reports that Israeli forces and settlers have killed Palestinian children and teenagers in the occupied West Bank at an average of about seven a month since October 2023, against roughly one a month before. Families say Israeli military investigations rarely produce accountability; the Israeli military says it investigates such deaths.
Israel's far-right national security minister publicly boasts of having worsened prison conditions for Palestinian security prisoners.

The Straits Times publishes an analysis of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's position on settler violence, noting he condemned the Qusra attack while continuing to back far-right coalition partners. No new strikes or casualties were reported in Gaza or Lebanon in the preceding 24 hours.

The UK Foreign Office says it has raised with Israeli authorities the detention of Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old British student activist forcibly detained by Israeli settlers in Umm al-Kheir in the occupied West Bank on Saturday before being arrested.

An Israeli strike killed at least five Palestinians in Gaza on Monday, health officials say: two killed and several wounded when a strike hit a crowd near the municipal public park in Gaza City, an area densely populated with displaced families, and at least three more killed later when a strike hit a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighbourhood. The Israeli military said it targeted Hamas militants in the first strike and did not immediately comment on the second. Casualty figures come from Gaza health officials.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Israel and Greece sign a EUR 3 billion (S$4.43 billion) agreement under which Israel will build a multi-layered air defence system for Greece, named "Achilles Shield", to be delivered by 2036. Israel's defence ministry confirmed the signing.

Raam leader Mansour Abbas announces that Yoav Segalovitz, a former Israeli police official and until recently a Yesh Atid member of the Knesset, will run on the moderate Islamist party's list in the 27 October election — the first Jewish Israeli to stand for an explicitly Arab party. Raam will campaign on an anti-crime platform. Segalovitz said there is “a difficult history between Arabs and Jews in this country, but there is also a shared future”.

An Israeli-backed raid to detain a Hamas figure in Gaza City is discovered mid-operation. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz says a senior Hamas member was captured, and an Israeli security official says the man detained heads Hamas's internal security service. Gaza officials and medics say air strikes launched to cover the force's withdrawal killed at least four people near the Katiba area of western Gaza City — two children and a woman among them — with another child killed in central Gaza; witnesses described at least 12 missiles fired into an area crowded with displaced families. Hamas government media office director Ismail al-Thawabta says the Israeli unit was detected before it could finish. Casualty figures come from Gaza medical sources and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Israeli defence ministry, Gaza medics, Hamas media office)

timeline.event: Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar warns Israel will retaliate if the UK imposes sanctions over the potential expansion of West Bank settlements. The warning came shortly after British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Parliament he would introduce a 'comprehensive reset' of policy on Israel in the coming weeks, including examining how to stop UK companies financing, constructing or advertising new settlements.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accuses security officials of deliberately failing to wake him on the morning of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, insisting the assault would have been contained had he intervened earlier - a day after his wife claimed an opposition figure knew of the attack in advance, prompting a threatened lawsuit. Netanyahu faces close-fought elections later in 2026. The 7 October attack killed more than 1,200 people in Israel and saw 251 taken hostage; Gaza authorities report more than 73,000 Palestinians killed in the offensive that followed.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli and Gaza authorities)

timeline.event: Unifil says the Israeli military has established four new bases in the areas of southern Lebanon it invaded, bringing the number of Israeli positions to nine, and reports consolidation and fortification of those positions along with demolition and engineering work. The strip under Israeli control is about 5 per cent of Lebanese territory and extends up to 10km from the border in places. A Lebanese intelligence official says Lebanon's military has recorded more than 5,000 violations of the June deal by Israel; the Israeli military says the buildings destroyed were used by Hezbollah for military purposes and that it acts in accordance with international law.
timeline.source: BBC (Unifil, Lebanese intelligence official, Israeli military)

timeline.event: More than 10 EU countries say they are willing to contribute to a planned European mission to train the Lebanese army.

Israel says a Hamas security chief was captured during a raid in Gaza City in which strikes killed four people, according to Gaza medics. Hezbollah's leader Naim Qassem last week called the US-brokered framework for the group's disarmament 'surrender with humiliation'.

Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry says Israeli attacks have killed more than 900 people in the territory so far in 2026 despite the ceasefire, taking the total since the 10 October truce past 1,300, including 301 children. The ministry does not separate civilians from combatants. The UN considers the figures reliable and BBC Verify says independent analysis is consistent with them; the Israeli military disputes the count, saying there is no basis to assume all those listed were killed by its activity, and says five of its soldiers have been killed in combat since the ceasefire.

A BBC team travelling with Unifil inside the part of southern Lebanon under Israeli control reports entire villages flattened, with air strikes and demolitions continuing after the ceasefire announced in June. Lebanese officials say Israel is expanding its positions in the zone.

Two Palestinian teenagers are killed in an attack by Israeli settler militants and army troops on their village in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, local officials and the Palestinian health ministry say, amid an uptick in settler violence in the territory. Israel has not published its own account.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Palestinian health ministry, local officials)

timeline.event: The Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, named after a Shi'ite scholar whose shrine sits at its summit, has become one of the most contested pieces of ground in the Israel-Hezbollah war, according to a Straits Times explainer from Beirut.

Netanyahu visits Israeli forces inside the Gaza Strip, his first trip there since the October 2025 ceasefire, and rejects mediators' push for a US-backed plan requiring withdrawal. 'We control the area. We are not retreating. We are staying on this line,' he says near the Yellow Line, adding that Israel controls 60 per cent of the strip. Hamas has not responded publicly to the visit.
Rights groups urge US lawmakers to drop a provision that would deepen American defence ties with Israel.
Lebanon receives the first of five Lebanese detainees Israel has agreed to free as part of continuing talks between the two governments.
The US House of Representatives passes a bill to penalise university boycotts of Israel. It still requires Senate action.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (US House of Representatives)

timeline.event: Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, campaigning ahead of close-fought elections, sets out a plan to remove Palestinians from Gaza: 250,000 in the first year and the remaining roughly two million over the following six. He claims unnamed countries are 'ready' to take them and says the plan does not amount to forcing anyone out. No government decision has been announced. Forced displacement of civilians in occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions.

The Israeli military says it has cleared Hezbollah fighters from tunnels beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, one of the most contested positions of the conflict. Hezbollah has not confirmed the account and the claim has not been independently verified.

With Israeli elections approaching, more of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition partners publicly back removing Palestinians from Gaza, after National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir set out a staged plan earlier in the day. Such proposals are opposed by Palestinian officials and by Israel's main mediators.
Thousands of Lebanese students remain displaced as the school year approaches, with schools in the south destroyed or occupied and families still unable to return home.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: DR Congo's Ebola epidemic added 92 confirmed cases and 33 deaths in a single day, and a new case surfaced in rebel-held North Kivu more than two months after the AFC/M23 declared its territory clear — a reminder that the parts of the country hardest to survey are the parts least likely to stay free of it. The United States is carrying two very different problems: a cyclosporiasis outbreak traced to imported iceberg lettuce that is now one of the largest foodborne outbreaks in decades, and a measles count that has held flat for a third week. Europe's board is seasonal rather than alarming, with West Nile cases climbing steadily through the mosquito season and a contained salmonella cluster in France. Indonesia's school-meal poisonings remain the most unsettling item, because roughly 2,000 people fell ill in three days and nobody has yet said why. For readers here, none of this is travel-blocking — but the DRC line is the one that keeps outrunning the official ledger.

outbreaks.name: DR Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: Still a Public Health Emergency of International Concern; new confirmed cases only in DR Congo
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO-confirmed cumulative figures as of 26 August, re-read this run from Disease Outbreak News 616 (published 28 August; the DON OData feed shows nothing newer): 5,794 cases in DR Congo including two patients later treated in Germany, plus 20 in Uganda and one in France, with 2,788 deaths including two in Uganda, and at least 1,314 recovered. The country count is the four countries with cases or treated patients on WHO's list — DR Congo, Uganda, France and Germany. DR Congo's own national series runs ahead of the WHO-ratified count: ECDC's outbreak page, refreshed today, cites the DRC situation report of 3 September (data to 2 September) at 6,342 confirmed cases and 3,072 deaths, up 92 cases and 33 deaths in a day, with 770 patients hospitalised in isolation, 1,475 recovered and 86.5 per cent of contacts under follow-up. Ituri accounts for 5,164 cases and 2,342 deaths, ahead of North Kivu (913/614), Haut-Uele (236/103), Tshopo (22/9), Bas-Uele (4/3) and South Kivu (3/1), across 60 of 151 health zones in six provinces. WHO declared Uganda's outbreak over on 25 August and DON 616 records the 42-day monitoring period as complete in Uganda and France. Ervebo vaccination of health workers began in DR Congo on 27 August, though protection against Bundibugyo virus in humans is unknown. This is the largest Ebola outbreak recorded in DR Congo.

outbreaks.name: United States — cyclosporiasis (iceberg lettuce)
outbreaks.status: Investigation still open; recalled product past its best-by dates
outbreaks.scope_note: CDC's outbreak page, last updated 3 September and read this run, counts 11,458 laboratory-confirmed cases across 20 states (three newly added), with 495 hospitalisations and two deaths. FDA and CDC linked the outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell restaurants on 16 July, and confirmed the next day that the lettuce came from Taylor Farms' Mexico operations; Taylor Farms recalled the product the same day. CDC notes the best-by dates have passed, so affected product should no longer be in stores or restaurants. This is one of the largest US foodborne outbreaks in decades.

outbreaks.name: Global — cholera
outbreaks.status: Still spreading across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas; Nigeria dominates the current wave
outbreaks.scope_note: Worldwide totals since 1 January 2026, re-read this run from the PDF of ECDC's week-35 Communicable Disease Threats Report of 28 August, still the newest issue in ECDC's feed. Between 27 July and 26 August, 42,717 new cases and 257 new deaths were reported; Nigeria alone accounted for 41,296 cases and 242 deaths, ahead of Angola (524), Somalia (489), Mozambique (319) and Chad (47). The country count is the 19 countries that reported new cases in that month. The previous reporting period, 22 June to 27 July, had 8,247 new cases and 326 deaths. The equivalent 2025 figure was 338,340 cases and 4,324 deaths. ECDC notes case definitions, testing strategies and reporting completeness vary widely, so the totals are an undercount.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus
outbreaks.status: Seasonal transmission still expanding; week 36 dashboard published today
outbreaks.scope_note: Locally acquired human cases in the 2026 season as at 3 September, re-read this run from ECDC's weekly West Nile dashboard, week 36, published 4 September. Italy leads with 516 cases, ahead of Greece on 284 (11 with unknown place of infection), Spain 88, Romania 56, North Macedonia 55, France 36, Serbia 18, the Netherlands nine, Croatia seven, Cyprus six, Austria four, Hungary three, Germany two, and Albania and Kosovo one each. Twenty areas were reported affected for the first time this season in the past week. The dashboard is built for blood-donor deferral decisions and does not publish a season death count, hence the dash.

outbreaks.name: United States — measles
outbreaks.status: Worst US year since elimination was declared in 2000; count unchanged for a third week
outbreaks.scope_note: CDC's confirmed 2026 count as of its 27 August data date, re-read from CDC's measles data page this run (page updated 30 August) and still the latest figure published: 2,887 cases reported by 47 jurisdictions plus cases among international visitors, across 37 new outbreaks declared in 2026. CDC's national total records no measles deaths; Pennsylvania separately reported two measles-associated deaths on 25 August that CDC says it is not counting while it reviews whether measles caused or contributed to them.

outbreaks.name: Indonesia — free school meals food poisoning
outbreaks.status: Suspected foodborne outbreak across multiple provinces; cause not yet identified
outbreaks.scope_note: Around 2,000 students and teachers fell ill over three days after eating meals from the government's Makan Bergizi Gratis programme, per BBC News Indonesia reporting of 3 September citing school and local health officials: 752 students and 25 teachers at a high school in Lasem, Rembang (Central Java) on Wednesday, 730 people at an Islamic boarding school in Sidoarjo (East Java) on Tuesday, and hundreds more across schools in Tana Toraja, South Sulawesi. The figure is a running total of locally reported cases, not a laboratory-confirmed national count; food samples are being tested and no cause has been announced. No deaths have been reported.

stories.headline: DR Congo's national Ebola count reaches 6,342 cases and 3,072 deaths
stories.summary: ECDC's outbreak page, refreshed today, cites the DRC situation report of 3 September (data to 2 September): 6,342 confirmed Bundibugyo virus cases and 3,072 deaths, an increase of 92 cases and 33 deaths in a single day. The new cases came from Ituri (60), North Kivu (25), Haut-Uele (five) and Tshopo (two). A total of 770 patients are hospitalised in isolation, 1,475 have recovered and 86.5 per cent of identified contacts are under follow-up. These national figures run ahead of the 5,815 cases and 2,788 deaths WHO has formally ratified in Disease Outbreak News 616; ECDC's next update is due 7 September.
stories.source: ECDC epidemiological update (DRC health ministry situation report)

stories.headline: New Ebola case detected in rebel-held eastern Congo, months after the area declared itself clear
stories.summary: AFC/M23 rebels, who control large parts of North and South Kivu, said a new Ebola case was confirmed in the Kayna health zone near Lubero — more than two months after they declared territory under their control Ebola-free following 21 days without a case. The patient, a 21-year-old man, had arrived from Butembo in government-held territory; it is not clear where he was infected. He was flagged at a health checkpoint on Wednesday, moved to a quarantine facility and confirmed positive the following day. Contact tracing has begun. Rebel-held areas had recorded only four cases since the outbreak was declared in mid-May. The account comes from the rebel group and has not been independently confirmed.

stories.headline: US cyclosporiasis outbreak reaches 11,458 cases as officials question the response
stories.summary: CDC's investigation into iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms' Mexico operations, updated 3 September, now counts 11,458 cases across 20 states with 495 hospitalisations and two deaths. The Straits Times reported from Washtenaw County, Michigan, where health staff dropped vaccination and restaurant-inspection duties to trace hundreds of patients. Michigan officials say they alerted federal agencies in late June and advised residents to avoid lettuce on 4 July — nearly two weeks before the FDA and CDC announcement on 16 July. Food-safety researchers quoted by ST argue the episode exposed how thin US outbreak-response capacity has become.
stories.source: US CDC, The Straits Times (FDA, Michigan health officials)

stories.headline: Salmonella outbreak linked to pumpkin seeds infects 81 people in France
stories.summary: France's health and agriculture ministries said a salmonella outbreak tied to a batch of pumpkin seeds infected 81 people across several regions between May and August. Six were hospitalised and two were attended by emergency services; all have since recovered. The investigation points to seeds processed by a company in south-western France and sold through several retailers, including the Grand Frais chain.
stories.source: The Straits Times (French health and agriculture ministries)

stories.headline: West Nile virus reaches 1,086 human cases across 15 European countries
stories.summary: ECDC's week-36 dashboard, published today with data to 3 September, counts 1,086 locally acquired human cases this season — up from 877 a week earlier. Italy accounts for 516 and Greece 284, followed by Spain (88), Romania (56) and North Macedonia (55). Twenty areas were reported affected for the first time this season in the past week. The dashboard exists to guide blood-donor deferral and does not publish a season death count.
stories.source: ECDC weekly West Nile virus surveillance dashboard, week 36

stories.headline: Around 2,000 people fall ill in Indonesia after eating free school meals
stories.summary: Roughly 2,000 students and teachers across Indonesia fell ill over three days after eating meals from President Prabowo Subianto's Makan Bergizi Gratis programme. The largest single case was in Lasem, Rembang, where 752 students and 25 teachers reported symptoms after Wednesday lunch and the school sent nearly 1,200 pupils home; 730 people fell ill at an Islamic boarding school in Sidoarjo the day before, and hundreds more across schools in Tana Toraja. Parents and teachers described slimy chicken and undercooked food; samples are being tested and local authorities are investigating.

stories.headline: WHO's latest Disease Outbreak News puts the DR Congo Ebola epidemic at 5,815 confirmed cases
stories.summary: Disease Outbreak News 616, published 28 August and still the newest on this outbreak, records 5,815 confirmed Bundibugyo virus cases and 2,788 deaths as of 26 August, with new confirmed cases now reported only in DR Congo. At least 1,314 patients have recovered. The 42-day enhanced monitoring period completed in both France and Uganda on 27 August. WHO says sustained transmission in DR Congo means the risk of further exportation remains, and notes that vaccination of health workers with Ervebo began on 27 August even though its protection against Bundibugyo virus in humans is unknown.

stories.headline: Global cholera adds 42,717 cases in a month, four in five of them in Nigeria
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 threats report counts 212,857 cholera cases and 1,943 deaths worldwide since 1 January, including 42,717 new cases and 257 deaths between 27 July and 26 August. Nigeria accounted for 41,296 of those cases and 242 of the deaths, ahead of Angola, Somalia, Mozambique and Chad. The monthly total is more than five times the previous reporting period's 8,247 cases, though last year's running total at the same point was higher at 338,340.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch Chrome first: Google shipped an emergency fix for a V8 type-confusion zero-day (CVE-2026-85046, CVSS 8.8) that is already being exploited through malicious web pages. After that the queue is edge devices and build infrastructure — a 9.8 unauthenticated root RCE in Cisco Nexus 9000 switches, a matching 9.8 in HPE's ArubaOS-CX, and two SonicWall SMA 1000 zero-days that CISA added to its known-exploited catalog alongside five others this week. The week's real theme is that attackers are going after the plumbing that delivers software rather than the software itself: Coder's module registry was hijacked via its Cloudflare configuration to serve credential-stealing Terraform modules for 14 hours, and a BGP hijack pushed a trojanised Virtualizor update straight to hosting servers. WordPress operators have their own homework, with roughly 3.25 million sites still running an unpatched backup plugin and over 440,000 exploit attempts logged against Elementor Pro. If you run a build pipeline, assume any token reachable from it needs rotating rather than auditing.

stories.headline: Google patches an actively exploited Chrome V8 zero-day
stories.summary: Google shipped Chrome 152.0.7977.82/.83 for Windows and macOS and 152.0.7977.82 for Linux to fix a type-confusion flaw in the V8 JavaScript engine that it says is being exploited in the wild. A malicious web page can corrupt memory and run code. It is the sixth actively exploited Chrome bug patched in 2026; the same release fixed 11 other issues, nine of them high severity. The flaw was reported by researcher Salvatore Gulizia. NVD rates it 8.8.

stories.headline: More than 440,000 exploit attempts target Elementor Pro and Super Forms RCE flaws
stories.summary: Attackers are mass-scanning WordPress sites for a file-upload flaw in Elementor Pro 4.2.1 and earlier that lets them plant a PHP webshell in the plugin's forms upload directory and run commands on the server. Exploitation needs a published Form widget with a file-upload field, a common configuration across the plugin's 6 million-plus installs. Fixed in 4.2.2. The Hacker News counts over 440,000 attempts across Elementor Pro and Super Forms; BleepingComputer reported 190,000 blocked against Elementor alone.

stories.headline: Plex tells users to update immediately after patching undisclosed flaws
stories.summary: Plex emailed users directly - a step it reserves for serious advisories - urging an immediate upgrade to Media Server 1.43.3 and Desktop 1.115.0. The company has not described the bugs and no CVE IDs have been assigned yet; it says it has requested CVE records. Anything running Media Server 1.43.2 or earlier is affected, and NAS package managers may lag the official release, so Plex is pointing users to manual installers.

stories.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra scores 100% on ExploitBench as the company blocks proof-of-concept exploit requests
stories.summary: OpenAI's new model reached a perfect score on the ExploitBench offensive-security benchmark, and the company simultaneously began refusing requests to write proof-of-concept exploits. The pairing is the clearest signal yet that frontier models can now automate exploit development, and that vendors are treating that capability as something to gate rather than advertise.

stories.headline: French hospital fined 500,000 euros after a breach exposed data on 727,000 people
stories.summary: France's data protection regulator fined a hospital 500,000 euros over a breach affecting 727,000 people, citing failures in access control and monitoring. The penalty is one of the larger healthcare-sector fines issued in Europe this year.

stories.headline: Coder's module registry hijacked to serve credential-stealing Terraform modules
stories.summary: An attacker got into Coder's Cloudflare configuration and added rogue IP addresses to the pool serving registry.coder.com, then delivered malicious Terraform modules for roughly 14 hours on Aug 31 (07:35-21:45 UTC). The modules harvested provisioner environment variables, cloud API keys, CI/CD credentials, SSH keys, OIDC tokens and database passwords, exfiltrating to coder-infra[.]com. Coder shipped 2.37.0, 2.36.4, 2.35.7 and 2.34.9 and says it cannot identify every affected deployment - rotate credentials and check firewall logs.

stories.headline: HPE patches a critical unauthenticated RCE in ArubaOS-CX switches
stories.summary: A buffer overflow in an ArubaOS-CX daemon lets an unauthenticated remote attacker send crafted packets and execute code with elevated privileges on enterprise switches. Affected builds include 10.18.0001, 10.17.1021, 10.16.1051, 10.13.1180 and 10.10.1180 and earlier. HPE says it is not aware of exploitation or public proof-of-concept code; the same bulletin covers 23 further flaws rated 8.1 to 8.8.

stories.headline: Critical Cisco Nexus 9000 flaw lets unauthenticated attackers run code as root
stories.summary: The Silicon One integration on Cisco Nexus 9000 switches leaves TCP ports 43210 and 43211 reachable in the default Layer 3 VRF, and crafted input to that service is executed with root privileges. Cisco found the bug while working a support case and says its PSIRT is not aware of malicious use. Fixed NX-OS builds are available; Cisco has also tested an infrastructure access control list workaround for sites that cannot patch immediately.

stories.headline: BraZetsu malware turns compromised Windows hosts into criminal marketplace inventory
stories.summary: Researchers describe a campaign that enrolls infected Windows machines into a marketplace where access to them is sold on, rather than monetising each victim directly. The model shortens the path from initial infection to hands-on-keyboard intrusion by a second actor.

stories.headline: Thomson Reuters court software breach may have exposed Social Security numbers and sealed records
stories.summary: Thomson Reuters disclosed that an unauthorised party took files from C-Track, the court case-management platform sold by its West Publishing unit, in March 2026; the activity was discovered on Jun 30. Appellate courts in 11 US states and the US Virgin Islands are affected, along with three Ontario courts. Exposed records may include names, Social Security numbers, driver's licence numbers, dates of birth and medical and health-insurance information, and at some courts confidential, redacted or sealed material. Affected individuals are being offered 12 months of credit monitoring.
stories.source: The Hacker News, Help Net Security, The Record (Thomson Reuters, West Publishing)

stories.headline: US is the top target in an RMM phishing campaign spanning 46 countries
stories.summary: A phishing operation tracked across 46 countries pushes victims to install legitimate remote monitoring and management tools, giving operators hands-on access without deploying malware that endpoint products would flag. US organisations account for the largest share of targeting.

stories.headline: Attackers turn the trusted Node.js runtime into a malware delivery tool
stories.summary: In targeted intrusions, attackers are shipping a signed Node.js binary and running their payload as a script through it, so execution happens under a legitimate, commonly allow-listed runtime. Defenders relying on binary reputation alone will miss it.

stories.headline: Shai-Hulud's credential harvesting grows to 469 locations
stories.summary: The Shai-Hulud npm worm now searches 469 distinct credential locations on infected developer machines and CI runners, up sharply from earlier variants. Anyone who ran an affected package should treat every token reachable from that host as compromised.

stories.headline: Pegasus zero-click exploit infects a Serbian student activist's iPhone
stories.summary: Researchers found NSO Group's Pegasus on the iPhone of a member of Serbia's student protest movement, delivered without any interaction from the target. It is the latest in a documented pattern of commercial spyware being used against civil society in the region.

stories.headline: Researcher publishes FalconFlank proof-of-concept for privilege escalation in CrowdStrike Falcon
stories.summary: A researcher released working proof-of-concept code, dubbed FalconFlank, demonstrating local privilege escalation against the CrowdStrike Falcon agent. Public exploit code for an EDR agent raises the value of any foothold on a protected host.

stories.headline: CISA adds seven actively exploited flaws to the KEV catalog
stories.summary: Catalog version 2026.09.02 added seven entries, taking the KEV list to 1,694: both SonicWall SMA1000 flaws (CVE-2026-83548, SSRF, NVD 10.0; CVE-2026-83549, OS command injection, 7.8), JFrog Artifactory improper authentication (CVE-2026-82329, 9.8), Sangoma Switchvox SQL injection (CVE-2026-9586, 9.8), Kestra OSS command injection (CVE-2026-49869, 10.0), BerriAI LiteLLM improper authentication (CVE-2026-59822, 8.2) and Kludex Starlette request smuggling (CVE-2026-48710, 6.5). The Hacker News reports attackers deploying reverse shells and crypto miners through them. The CVSS shown is the highest in the set.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV catalog, NVD

stories.headline: WordPress backup plugin flaw exposes millions of sites to takeover
stories.summary: A second-order SQL injection in All-in-One WP Migration and Backup lets an unauthenticated attacker plant malicious data via WordPress trackbacks that fires when an administrator later restores a backup, leading to remote code execution and full site takeover. Versions up to 7.109 are affected; 7.110 shipped on Aug 20. Of more than 5 million installs, roughly 3.25 million are still unpatched.

stories.headline: Fake software installers disable Windows Update and weaken Microsoft Defender
stories.summary: Trojanised installers for popular applications are turning off Windows Update and degrading Defender's protections before dropping their payload, leaving the host unpatched and under-monitored for whatever follows.

stories.headline: Malicious .git configs can make Claude, Codex, Cursor and other AI coding agents run attacker code
stories.summary: Researchers showed that a hostile repository's .git configuration can coerce AI coding agents - Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's Codex, Cursor and others - into executing attacker-supplied commands when a developer points the agent at the repo. Cloning untrusted code into an agent's working directory should now be treated as running it.

stories.headline: BGP hijack delivers a malicious Virtualizor update that establishes persistent root access
stories.summary: Attackers hijacked BGP routes to intercept traffic to a Virtualizor update endpoint and serve a trojanised package, giving them persistent root on hosting servers that pulled it. Routing-layer interception defeats the usual assumption that a vendor's update URL reaches the vendor.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit two SonicWall SMA 1000 zero-days that may chain together
stories.summary: Two flaws in SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances are being exploited in the wild and may form an attack chain: a server-side request forgery rated 10.0 by NVD (CVE-2026-83548) and an OS command injection rated 7.8 (CVE-2026-83549). Both were added to CISA's KEV catalog on Sep 2. These appliances sit at the network edge, so patching is urgent.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD (SonicWall)

stories.headline: GeoNetwork fixes an unauthenticated RCE chain affecting government geoportal backends
stories.summary: The open-source catalog software behind many national and municipal geoportals patched a chain that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach remote code execution on the backend. Public-sector deployments are the primary exposure.

stories.headline: Researchers use Claude to port a pre-auth RCE exploit from one PLC model to another
stories.summary: A research team used Anthropic's Claude to adapt a working pre-authentication remote code execution exploit from one programmable logic controller to a different model, compressing work that normally needs deep familiarity with each device. The result matters for ICS owners who rely on hardware diversity as a defence.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit a critical Sangoma Switchvox flaw to deploy reverse shells without credentials
stories.summary: An SQL injection in Sangoma's Switchvox VoIP platform is being used to drop reverse shells on unauthenticated systems. NVD rates it 9.8 and CISA added it to the KEV catalog on Sep 2.
stories.source: The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: Authorities turn Sality's peer-to-peer network against itself to cut off new payloads
stories.summary: Investigators used the long-running Sality botnet's own peer-to-peer update mechanism to stop infected machines receiving new malware, disrupting the network without seizing central infrastructure it does not have.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit a critical JFrog Artifactory flaw to mint admin tokens days after disclosure
stories.summary: An improper authentication flaw in JFrog Artifactory lets attackers issue administrative tokens, handing them control of the build artifacts an organisation ships. Exploitation began within days of disclosure and CISA added the CVE to the KEV catalog on Sep 2; NVD rates it 9.8.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: Thirteen malicious Packagist packages target unpatched iPhones to steal crypto wallet seeds
stories.summary: Thirteen packages published to the PHP package repository Packagist chained to an exploit for unpatched iPhones and attempted to extract cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases. The packages have been removed.

stories.headline: Iranian hackers pose as recruiters to deliver cross-platform RATs through coding tests
stories.summary: An Iran-linked group is approaching targets with fake job offers and sending remote access trojans disguised as take-home coding assignments, with payloads for Windows, macOS and Linux. Engineers at defence, telecom and research organisations are the stated targets.
